THE RULES OF THE ROAD

Click. Drive. Brake.

  1. One click takes your turn. Click the exact grid cell where you want to land. The 3×3 matrix is centered on your position plus your current velocity. It appears only when a human can drive. Green is clear; red means a crash. Hover to preview the path.
  2. Build speed, then brake. Each surrounding square adds −1, 0 or +1 to your velocity on each axis. Choose against your velocity to brake. The center, S or Space keeps your momentum. For example, moving right by 2 cells gives rightward landing choices 1, 2 or 3 cells away. Start by heading right →, then follow the arrows clockwise.
  3. Watch the entire path. Potholes, track edges and cars cause a crash even when your destination is clear. Only the moving car stops.
  4. Jump the gap. Drive straight along the yellow ramp's arrow with enough speed to jump the next cell and land beyond it. You can jump a hole or another car.
  5. Crashes limit speed. The car travels to the impact and stops on the last safe road cell. You can drive on your very next turn, with a speed limit of 1 grid cell for 3 turns (including diagonal steps). There are no skipped turns. Normal acceleration returns afterward. AI follows the same rules.
  6. A living world. Pick Forest, Desert, Futuristic, Jungle, Sky, Sea or Space before racing. Each world has its own scenery, crash effects and hidden-route trails. Birds and probes land and take off; creatures and rovers cross the road. Help and the menu pause them; reduced-motion mode keeps them still.
  7. Finish one full lap. Pass three checkpoints and cross the finish line clockwise. Backing over the line does not win.
  8. Watch for wildlife. Ending a move on a grounded animal, landed drone or rover causes a crash. Passing its cell is safe. Flying animals are clear of the road. An animal walking onto a parked car never triggers a crash. The landing warning updates as wildlife moves.
